title: OKRs fault-tolerance matrix and initiative fallback playbook
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Goal: Build a conservative, testable framework that maps company-level OKRs to a fault-tolerant set of initiative responses, so we can maintain objective velocity despite cross-functional outages, resourcing shocks, or model/regulatory regressions.

Scope:
- Define a decision matrix that specifies automated and human-triggered fallback actions per OKR (e.g., degrade feature surface, pause non-critical rollouts, throttle Dedicated capacity).
- Create an initiative-level ‘criticality’ taxonomy and restore/prioritization rules that product, ENG, and SRE can apply during stress events.
- Integrate with release gating (Console rollouts) and the capacity planner so we can run what-if simulations for quarterly planning cycles.
- Produce a lightweight runbook and a CS/Support escalation ladder for high-impact customers.

Deliverables:
1) Fault-tolerance matrix CSV + visualization in the OKR dashboard.
2) Initiative criticality taxonomy doc (Confluence) and acceptance criteria.
3) Playbook: automated fallbacks (runtime route changes, model variant switches) + manual rollback procedures.
4) Simulation harness for capacity/resourcing shock tests (local and staging).
5) Training session for PM/ENG/SRE and an on-call checklist.

Success criteria:
- For every Company-level OKR, a fallback plan exists and is tested via an injected failure simulation in at least one cycle.
- We can surface the next prioritized initiative within 2 hours of a major capacity or SLO degradation.
- Post-incident customer-impact percentage reduced by at least 30% vs baseline (measured on prior incidents).
comments: 2025-01-12: Kickoff with cross-functional reps (Product, SRE, Runtime, Customer Success). Agreed scope and owners. Action: Samira to draft taxonomy outline by 2025-01-17.

2025-01-18: Draft taxonomy posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/okrs/initiative-criticality-draft. Feedback from SRE: include 'regional capacity' as separate axis. Assigned follow-up to ENG lead (PR-4621).

2025-01-23: Decision in sync: use three criticality bands (Tier A: customer-facing SLA; Tier B: revenue-driving but degraded tolerable; Tier C: exploratory/low-risk). Liam to own mapping for Dedicated and Private offerings.
2025-01-28: Prototype matrix uploaded (CSV) and visualized on dashboard: https://analytics.redwood.ai/d/okr/fault-tolerance-matrix. Early flag: some mid-priority initiatives lack operator runbooks.

2025-01-30: Trade-off discussion: aggressive automated fallback reduces customer disruptions but may impact perceived feature parity. PMs prefer manual approval for Tier A. Document updated with approval gating rules: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcExample.

2025-02-01: Integration test planned for 2025-02-08: simulate a regional capacity outage for model-batching engine and verify automated fallback to quantized variant + scaled-down batch size. Linked PR implementing simulation harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342.
2025-02-01: Next steps: finalize playbook, run tabletop with execs, and schedule a 60-minute training with PS and SRE week of 2025-02-15.
